title: Signature Forest Canopy Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Forest Canopy cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its case is a layered canopy of carved leaves in three depths, with the bird appearing from a hollow branch rather than a door.

Mechanism: A weight-driven movement with bellows and pipes makes the standard two-note call, and the bird slides from its branch hollow on a rail. The leaf pendulum is carved as a single oak leaf on a slim rod.

Maintenance: Hang the clock level, wind it daily or weekly according to its movement, and brush the layered leaves with a soft brush. Keep the branch hollow free of dust so the bird slides freely.

Build and restoration: The branch rail is reached from the case back for cleaning. Tools: soft brush, screwdrivers, oil, tweezers, and a wall screw rated for the load.

title: Signature Alpine Chalet Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Alpine Chalet cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its chalet has a snow-capped roof, a balcony with a turning mill wheel, and shutters that open with the call.

Mechanism: The weight-driven cuckoo movement drives the bird and the mill wheel, which turns while the clock calls. The movement is a standard eight-day design with pinecone weights.

Maintenance: Hang the chalet level and clear of the wall so the wheel turns freely, and wind weekly. Brush snow and roof details with a soft brush, never a cloth that snags.

Build and restoration: The wheel bearing is oiled sparingly from the case back. Tools: soft brush, oil, screwdrivers, tweezers, and a spirit level.

title: Signature Nightingale Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Nightingale cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Instead of the two-note cuckoo call it plays a longer nightingale phrase on three pipes, while a nightingale figure appears in place of the cuckoo.

Mechanism: Three bellows and three pipes produce the phrase in sequence, driven by a cam with three lifts on the bird train. The going train is a standard weight-driven leaf-pendulum movement.

Maintenance: Keep all three bellows airtight and the pipes tuned, since a weak pipe spoils the phrase. Wind on schedule and keep the clock level.

Build and restoration: The three pipes are tuned by their stoppers against a pitch reference. Tools: bellow leather, pipe stoppers, tuning reference, tweezers, and oil.

title: Signature Woodland Workshop Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Woodland Workshop cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its case is a tiny workshop with a woodchopper who saws while the clock calls, and tools carved along the case front.

Mechanism: The woodchopper is driven by a lever from the bird train, sawing back and forth in time with the call. The going and bird trains are standard weight-driven cuckoo trains.

Maintenance: Keep the saw arm's pivot clean and free, and brush the carved tools with a soft brush. Wind on schedule and hang the clock level.

Build and restoration: The saw lever is reached from the case back and its pivot is oiled sparingly. Tools: soft brush, oil, tweezers, screwdrivers, and small clamps.

title: Signature Minimalist Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Minimalist cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its case is a plain beech rectangle with no carving, a single round dial, and the bird appearing from a flush door that is invisible when closed.

Mechanism: The movement is a standard weight-driven cuckoo movement with bellows and pipes, hidden entirely behind the plain case front. The pendulum is a plain rod with a disc bob.

Maintenance: Wipe the plain case with a dry cloth weekly and wind on schedule. The flush door needs its hinges kept clean so it closes invisibly.

Build and restoration: The door hinges are adjusted with a single screw each. Tools: dry cloth, screwdrivers, oil, and a spirit level.

title: Signature Eight-Day Grand Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Eight-Day Grand cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. It is the largest Signature cuckoo design, 60 centimetres tall, with an eight-day movement, a musical train, and dancers that turn on the hour.

Mechanism: Three trains run the going, the bird call, and the music with dancers, all weight- or spring-driven from heavy pinecone weights. The music cylinder plays after the call, and the dancers turn until the tune ends.

Maintenance: Wind weekly, hang the clock on a fixing rated for its full weight, and keep the music comb dust-free. Level the clock carefully, since its size makes any tilt show in the beat.

Build and restoration: The three trains are laid out side by side for servicing. Tools: screwdrivers, oil, tweezers, tuning file, and a wall-fixing gauge.

title: Signature Bellows-Choir Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Bellows-Choir cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. It uses four bellows and four pipes to sound a four-note chord phrase on the hour, with two birds appearing together.

Mechanism: A cam with four lifts drives the four bellows in sequence, and the two birds bow in turn as their notes sound. The going train is a standard weight-driven leaf-pendulum movement.

Maintenance: Keep all four bellows airtight, since one leaking bellow breaks the chord. Tune the pipes as a set, not one at a time, against a pitch reference.

Build and restoration: The pipe stoppers are reached from the movement back and set as a chord. Tools: bellow leather, pipe stoppers, tuning reference, tweezers, and oil.

title: Signature Dancer's Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Dancer's cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. On the hour the bird calls and a pair of dancers on a balcony turn to a short music-box tune.

Mechanism: The music train is spring-driven and released by the bird train after the call, turning the dancer platform through a worm gear while the pinned cylinder plays. The going train is weight-driven as usual.

Maintenance: Keep the dancer platform bearing clean and the music comb dust-free. Wind the music spring on the hour schedule and the weights on their schedule.

Build and restoration: The platform bearing is oiled sparingly from below. Tools: oil, tweezers, tuning file, screwdrivers, and a pitch reference.

title: Signature Tide-and-Season Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Tide-and-Season cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its dial adds a tide ring and a season ring that turn slowly through the year, alongside the usual cuckoo call.

Mechanism: The tide and season rings are driven from the motion work through reduction trains, and corrected by hand against tide tables and the calendar. The going train is a weight-driven leaf-pendulum movement.

Maintenance: Correct the tide ring weekly and the season ring monthly. Wind on schedule and keep the clock level.

Build and restoration: The rings lift off the dial for cleaning without stripping the movement. Tools: tide table, calendar, screwdrivers, oil, and a soft brush.

title: Signature Traveller's Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Traveller's cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. It is a compact cuckoo, 25 centimetres tall, with locking weights, a clamped pendulum, and a carrying case for travel.

Mechanism: The weights lock against the case with a lever, and the pendulum clamps to a felt pad, so nothing swings in transit. The movement is a standard one-day weight-driven cuckoo movement in miniature.

Maintenance: Always lock the weights and clamp the pendulum before travel, and unlock them only after the clock is level on its new wall. Wind after travel, since a journey can let the weights down unevenly.

Build and restoration: The locks are adjusted with single screws. Tools: screwdrivers, felt pads, oil, and a spirit level.

title: Signature Moonlit Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Moonlit cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its dial is painted as a night sky, and a moon disc behind an aperture shows the moon's phase, while the bird calls on the hour as usual.

Mechanism: The moon disc is driven by a 59-tooth wheel from the motion work, advancing one tooth per day. The bird train and bellows are standard cuckoo design, and the night dial is painted, not luminous.

Maintenance: Set the moon disc from a known new moon and correct it every two to three years. Keep the painted dial out of sunlight to protect the night-sky paint.

Build and restoration: The disc lifts off for repainting without stripping the movement. Tools: fine brushes, moonphase paint, tweezers, and a lunar calendar.

title: Signature Mill-Wheel Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Mill-Wheel cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. A waterwheel beside the case turns while the clock calls, driven from the bird train, and a tiny miller figure tips his hat at the end of the call.

Mechanism: The wheel is turned by a gear from the bird train arbor, and the miller is tipped by a lever at the end of the call sequence. The going train is a standard weight-driven leaf-pendulum movement.

Maintenance: Keep the wheel bearing clean and free, and brush the mill and figure with a soft brush. Wind on schedule and hang the clock level so the wheel clears the wall.

Build and restoration: The wheel gear is reached from the case back. Tools: soft brush, oil, tweezers, screwdrivers, and small clamps.

title: Signature Waterfall Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Waterfall cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. A carved waterfall panel beside the dial carries a turning wheel that suggests falling water while the clock calls.

Mechanism: The wheel is driven from the bird train through a reduction gear, turning slowly during the call and stopping afterwards. The going train is a standard weight-driven cuckoo movement.

Maintenance: Keep the wheel free of dust and its bearing oiled sparingly. Wind on schedule and hang the clock level.

Build and restoration: The waterfall wheel lifts off its arbor for cleaning. Tools: soft brush, oil, tweezers, screwdrivers, and a spirit level.

title: Signature Clockmaker's Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Clockmaker's cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its case front is glazed so the movement, bellows and pipes can be watched at work, and the bird appears through a glazed door.

Mechanism: The movement is a standard weight-driven cuckoo movement on an open frame, with the bellows visible beside the pipes. The glass does not affect the call or the timekeeping, but it makes faults visible.

Maintenance: Clean the glass with a dry microfibre cloth and keep fingers off the bellows leather. Service intervals are the same as for a closed-case cuckoo clock.

Build and restoration: The glazed panels lift out on brass clips. Tools: microfibre cloth, screwdrivers, oil, tweezers, and bellow leather.

title: Signature Service-Friendly Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Service-Friendly cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. Its movement slides out on rails, its bellows are held by clips, and a service card inside the case lists every part size.

Mechanism: The movement is a standard weight-driven cuckoo movement, laid out so every wheel, bellow and pipe is reachable from the back without removing the dial. No special tool is needed beyond standard clockmaker's tools.

Maintenance: Follow the five-year service interval on the card and record each service. Replacement bellows and chains are standard sizes, so worn parts swap without remaking.

Build and restoration: The service card lists chain pitch, bellow size, and pipe pitches. Tools: screwdrivers, tweezers, oil, chain tool, and the case card.

title: Signature Grand Festival Cuckoo Clock
body:
Specifications: The Signature Grand Festival cuckoo clock is an original Signature design, not an authentic historical clock. It is the largest Signature cuckoo design, with a carved festival scene, two birds, a musical train, and dancers, all sounding and moving on the hour.

Mechanism: Four trains run the going, the two bird calls, and the music with dancers, driven by heavy weights and a music spring. The festival scene is carved around the case front and does not touch the movement.

Maintenance: Wind weekly, hang the clock on a fixing rated for its full weight, and keep the music comb and dancers dust-free. Level the clock carefully, since its size shows any tilt in the beat.

Build and restoration: The four trains are laid out side by side for servicing in order. Tools: screwdrivers, oil, tweezers, tuning file, and a wall-fixing gauge.
